title: tier-2 shipped code: CMF build-154504 key against CmfKey154504 (0x142e48a20)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-tank/src/manifest.rs, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-tank/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the cmf_key_154504 entry. The ledger binds the verdict to manifest.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is CmfKey154504 at exe 0x142e48a20 (v2b 0x7ff7c7b68a20). Signature: (Header*, uint8 out[32], int len); the header is passed in RCX and not read. The 512-byte table is the client's global at exe 0x1436100c0 (v2b 0x7ff7c83300c0), supplied as the unit state and read by the key routine.

The real body sits behind the client's overlapping-instruction opaque-predicate prologue. The emulator executes the same real path a normal call takes; the prologue only shuffles ESP, and the security cookie is written and checked around it.

The key routine seeds the cursor from table[0x100 + len] (len is 32, so table[0x120]), writes table[SignedMod(cursor, 512)] and advances the 32-bit cursor by 3. The client's SignedMod sequence (AND 0x800001ff plus the sign fix-ups) is exactly cursor & 511; the shipped signed_mod does the same on the truncated 32-bit value.

The table is synthetic, not game data: (i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF with table[0x120] = 162, table[162] = 0x00 and table[255] = 0xFF. The walk is 162, 165, ..., 255, so it reads 32 distinct indices, exercises table bytes 0x00 and 0xFF, and covers all 32 output bytes. The untouched header and a per-case output fill prove the routine writes every key byte.

The seed is a table byte, so this routine's cursor stays in 0..348 and cannot reach the 512 boundary or a negative i32 value. The % 512 wrap and the signed edge belong to the IV routine, whose cursor is 16 * buildVersion.

Mutation: the line-oriented mutator produces one mutant here - the seed offset 0x100 + 32 -> 0x100 - 32, which reads table[0xE0] = 0x6B - and the first key byte kills it. The differential, not the mutation stage, is what pins the 32-byte walk for this table.

Coverage gate is 0: the harness's linear sweep desynchronises at the overlapping-instruction opaque-predicate JMP in the entry prologue, so the discovered branch sites are the padding stubs, not the real body. The measured coverage is recorded in the ledger; the differential and mutation stages carry the unit.

acknowledgedGaps.what: Branch coverage of the client entry
acknowledgedGaps.why: The linear sweep cannot follow the overlapping-instruction opaque-predicate prologue, so it reports the padding branches rather than the real loop. The coverage value is still measured and recorded; the gate is 0. The 364-case differential and the mutation stage carry the unit.
